caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 46 of 2019
lawyer:
Momtazuddin Fakir, Additional Attorney General, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record --------- For the Petitioner 
A.M. Aminuddin, Senior Advocates (with Qumrul Haque Siddique, Advocate) instructed by Madhumaloty Chowdhury Barua, Advocate-on-Record ---------- For the Respondents
parties:
The State, represented by the Deputy, Commissioner, Dhaka ------- Petitioner
-Vs-
Sufia Begum and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J. This Petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 09.12.2018 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5564 of 2018 making the Rule absolute. 

 2. The relevant facts for the disposal of this petition, in short, are that Md. Kamal Uddin Chowdhury, Sheristader of Joint District Judge and Arbitration Court, Dhaka lodged a First Information Report with Kotwali Police Station against the accused Sufia Begum, Most. Razia Khatun and Shahidullah under sections 420/466/467/468/471 of the Penal Code alleging, inter alia, that he was directed to lodge the said F.I.R. against the accused persons bringing allegations of forging the plaint; judgment and decree of Title suit No. 455 of 1980 and Title Suit No. 550 of 1985 of the First Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka by manipulating the case record and also the allegation of forging the suit register keep in the office of Sheristader, First Assistant Judge's Court Dhaka. Earlier an inquiry officer, holding preliminary inquiry, submitted his report to the learned District Judge, Dhaka about the alleged forgery. Pursuant to the decision taken on the basis of inquiry report informant lodged the instant F.I.R. Accordingly, Kotwali Police Station Case No. 20(7) 17 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 268 of 2017 under sections 420/466/467/468/471 of the Penal Code was stated against the accused persons and the same is pending for holding investigation. 

 3. The respondents, challenging the initiation of the said case, filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the High Court Division and obtained Rule. The High Court Division by the impugned judgment made the said Rule absolute, thereby, quashed the proceeding by the impugned judgment and order. 

 5. Mr. Momtzauddin Fakir, learned Additional Attorney General appearing for the State, submits that the High Court Division has committed an error of law in quashing the proceeding inasmuch as the police report of the case has not yet been submitted and no proceeding is pending against the respondents as yet. He further submits that there is specific allegation against the respondents that they forged the plaint, judgment, decree and suit register of two Title Suits and, after holding preliminary enquiry finding prima facie case, the instant F.I.R. was lodged by the official of the Court, the High Court Division erred in law in quashing the case. 

 7. From the F.I.R. it appears that there is allegation against the respondents that they forged plaint, judgment and decree of Titles Suit No. 455 of 1980 and Title Suit No. 550 of 1985 of the First Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka. They also forged the suit registered kept in the office of Sheristadar of the First Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka. The investigation of the case has not yet been completed and the Court has not yet taken cognizance of the offence. So it is difficult to accept that a proceeding is pending against the respondents. 

 8. Mr. Qumrul Haque Siddique submits that the allegation against the respondents is that since they produced those documents in connection with a Title suit, that Court is only authorized to hold inquiry under section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and after disposal of the said suit that Court can file petition of com-plaint as per provision of section 195(1) (C) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. But in this case, it appears from the F.I.R. that the allegation against the respondents is that they themselves forged the plaint, judgment and decree of Title Suit Nos. 455 of 1980 and 550 of 1985 of the First Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka and also forged the suit register by manipulating Court's record. Holding preliminary inquiry it was found that all those case records have been manipulated. The High Court Division quashed the proceeding with the following words: 

 9. The aforesaid finding of the High Court Division cannot be a good ground for quashing a proceeding since the allegation against the respondents is that they themselves manipulated and forged the plaint, judgment and decree and concerned suit register of the aforesaid two suits in the office of Assistant Judge, Dhaka. In view of the facts and circumstances, it was not required for holding inquiry under section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and to file case as per provision of section 195(1) (c) of the code of Criminal Procedure.
